decisions.body: Decision A′, folded into the change artifacts on the task branch (commit f923f2e9): read design D4 as amended and D15–D18, proposal FR13–FR16 and the split NFR-S1, tasks 3.0, 3.0a, 3.3, 3.3a, 3.6, 5.1, 5.1a, 5.3, 6.3, 6.4, and the new deltas plugin/github-plugin, plugin/plugin-discovery. github-actions is a core built-in in the new module adapters/scm beside scm-status; the vendor bundle keeps the tracker only; the GitHub HTTP core moves to the library :githubapi and the egress allowlist to the leaf :httpegress (rule of two, manual-sync-pairs.md as revised on main). The pin survives as the describe flag checkIdIsPinnedPath. R1–R6, D13 and D14 stand. Resume fix-artifacts from the updated artifacts; the remaining MODIFIED blocks you listed are written.

decisions.body:
(1) Option A: a passing verdict keeps its below-threshold findings. Both premises behind the findings-less pass were checked: FR4 of add-stage-engine (findings are retry feedback) and FR8/D6 of add-manual-run (the exit code is the verdict, the file on exit 0 is ignored). D5 of this change removed the second one, and the first no longer holds alone: the state file, `status --json` and the usage report are consumers too. Industry practice is the same shape (GitHub code scanning records alerts below the failure threshold; Trivy separates --severity from --exit-code).

The decision is folded into the artifacts on the task branch, commit 924f92ac:
- design.md: D5 as amended, with the verified premises and the rejected alternative (narrowing the scenario); a new D9 row "The findings of a pass" with writers, readers and the enforcement
- proposal.md: FR7 extended
- tasks.md: 2.2a (Verdict.Pass(runUrl, findings); VerdictDerivation fills the below-threshold results; StateJsonMapper, AttemptMapper and UsageReportJsonMapper carry them through the existing findings field; CheckFindings.noteIgnoredOnPass deleted; a spec that a pass's findings feed no retry) and 2.2b (the same for the judge)
- specs/verification/verdict-executors: requirement "A pass keeps its below-threshold findings" with two scenarios

Note the second instance of the same defect, which the escalation did not list: JudgeVerdictExtractor returns an empty Pass on "passed": true. That is task 2.2b; the judge classes stay exempt from the derivation gate (D9, NG1).

(2) Option (a): main is fixed. #124 adds a reasoned exemption row for .gnomish/stages/usage-report/report.sh to UsageFoldOwnerBoundarySpec (the factory runs from the v0.1.0 release, which has no `usage --markdown`; the row is asserted reached, so it is deleted with the fold). main (#123, #124) is merged into the task branch as 15419d88. Do not re-touch the spec or the script.

Continue from task 2.2, then 2.2a and 2.2b.

lastEscalation.question:
migrate-verify-to-executor-contract: tasks 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 2.1 are done and verified (record: temporary-docs/gnomish/github-oinsio-gnomish-factory-121/implement.md). Two decisions block the rest.

(1) DESIGN GAP before task 2.2. Scenario verification/verdict-executors 'Warnings pass under the default threshold' (specs/verification/verdict-executors/spec.md:31-33) promises: shell exits 1, answer has only warning results -> 'the check passes with the warnings recorded as findings'. Verified premises: Verdict.Pass carries only runUrl (domain/engine/Verdict.java:36); StateJsonMapper writes findings=[] for a pass and reads none back (adapters/git/.../state/StateJsonMapper.java:221,251); today ShellCommandCheckRunner drops findings on exit 0 with a DEBUG note (CheckFindings.java:61). D5 and D9 name no owner for below-threshold findings on a pass; proposal NG2 (advisory severity) defers a related idea to harden-verification-integrity. Class: one instance (grep 'recorded as findings' in the change hits only this scenario). Alternative zero (no recording): the warnings are silently lost on every pass - a silent loss of a promised duty, the worst class. Options ranked: (A) Verdict.Pass gains List<Finding> (defensively copied); VerdictDerivation fills it with the below-threshold results; StateJsonMapper writes/reads the existing findings field for 'pass' (the wire field already exists, so no format change, only semantics); status/briefing/usage renderers keep treating Pass as passed. Owner stays VerdictDerivation, done inside 2.2; needs a D5 amendment via /opsx:update. (B) keep Pass findings-less and revise the scenario through /architect Mode C + /opsx:update (drop 'recorded as findings', or defer it to NG2's change) - this narrows a promise and needs the decision review. Recommendation: A.

(2) FINAL GATE RED ON MAIN, not caused by this change. bootstrap UsageFoldOwnerBoundarySpec 'no script under .gnomish/stages reduces tokens with jq' fails since 23435e81 (#122), which returned .gnomish/stages/usage-report/report.sh (lines 70-94) to its v0.1.0 jq reduce form. The implement stage may not edit .gnomish/ and may not weaken the gate, so root ./gradlew check (the stage's last check) stays red, and scoped PIT in :bootstrap cannot run (its coverage pass fails first). Options: (a) a human fixes main (report.sh or the spec, e.g. an allowlisted exemption for report.sh with its reason until the factory runs a release with usage --markdown) and the task branch is rebased/merged; (b) authorize this task to add that exemption row to UsageFoldOwnerBoundarySpec with the reason; (c) accept the red spec as known and let this change's final gate be judged without it.

Smaller notes for the same /opsx:update, if you take it: SarifLevel.passes in :executor-contract is a second pass derivation (to delete in 2.3); the new ResultLevel<->SarifLevel pair across the classpath barrier contradicts D8 'no new pair' and needs a manual-sync-pairs.md row; threat #35 in docs/sandbox-threat-registry.md ('poll platform-authored verdicts, not check-run statuses') conflicts with scm-status reading Checks + Commit Statuses (D3).
options: (1) A: Pass carries below-threshold findings, D5 amended, done in 2.2; (2) a: human fixes main
(1) A; (2) b: add a reasoned exemption row for report.sh in UsageFoldOwnerBoundarySpec within this task
(1) A; (2) c: accept the red spec, continue
(1) B: revise the scenario via /architect + /opsx:update; (2) as stated separately
